addedLinks.anchor: Original finish, replacement parts and past repairs
addedLinks.context: The model name is only the beginning. Original finish, replacement parts and past repairs, along with the way you sell, can all influence the outcome. You don’t need to become a guitar expert to make a good decision. You do need to know what to check and when to ask for help.

addedLinks.anchor: inherited an old guitar
addedLinks.context: You may have inherited an old guitar, rediscovered one in a closet, or decided to part with an instrument you’ve played for decades. These seven steps will help you prepare before accepting an offer.

addedLinks.anchor: Refinishing a worn guitar
addedLinks.context: For collectible instruments, the factory finish and original components can be a major part of the appeal. Refinishing a worn guitar or replacing aging hardware may reduce its value, even if the result looks cleaner. A professionally completed refret, however, deserves a different assessment from an irreversible modification such as cutting the body for larger pickups. Gruhn Guitars’ preservation advice explains the difference.

addedLinks.anchor: the visible signs of a guitar refinish
addedLinks.context: If you don't know whether the finish is original, start with the visible signs of a guitar refinish.

addedLinks.anchor: how replacement pickups and routing affect value
addedLinks.context: If the guitar already has replacement parts, it may still be desirable. The goal is to understand its present condition and price it accordingly. For changed electronics, see how replacement pickups and routing affect value.

addedLinks.context: Get an assessment before spending money to make an old guitar look new. Read whether restoration before selling makes sense before commissioning work.
